kaps_punt: Persoonlike sterkpunte: identifiseer, ondersoek en waardeer eie sterkpunte; ander se sterkpunte; suksesvolle ervarings as gevolg van eie sterkpunte; minder suksesvolle ervarings; maniere om minder suksesvolle ervarings in positiewe leerervarings te omskep

items.bewering: Nie elke kind in jou klas doen dieselfde dinge maklik nie. Daar is waarskynlik ook iets wat jy makliker doen as baie van hulle.
items.bron: VIA Institute on Character (viacharacter.org/character-strengths): everyone has all 24 strengths in different degrees, so every person's profile is unique. Manitoba Education, 'What Special Strengths Does My Child Have?' (edu.gov.mb.ca): children's strengths lie in different areas. The second sentence is hedged ('waarskynlik') and claims nothing absolute.

items.bewering: 'n Sterkpunt is iets wat jy goed doen en waarin jy nog beter kan word.
items.bron: Gallup CliftonStrengths, 'How to develop and improve strengths' (gallup.com): strength = talent x investment, and investment (practice, building skill) turns a talent into a strength and 'never ends'. Linley's definition (book review in the Brookes University journal, radar.brookes.ac.uk): a strength enables 'optimal functioning, development and performance'. Both say a strength is good performance that can still develop further, which is what the definition says.

items.bewering: Drie dinge help jou om jou eie sterkpunt raak te sien. Jy doen dit goed, jy geniet dit en maats vra jou hulp daarmee.
items.bron: UN Geneva learning, strengths session slides (learning.unog.ch): the 'strengths formula' is performance plus energy plus use, and a realised strength is one 'you are good at ... and you enjoy'. University of Edinburgh Careers Service (careers.ed.ac.uk/understand-yourself): ask the people around you what they see as your strengths. ManpowerGroup UK: when people regularly come to you for help with something, that often points to a strength. Checked as a set: all three are signs that help you recognise a strength, and the lesson does not say all three must be present. Sport, for example, seldom brings requests for help, and the text does not imply it should.

items.bewering: Party kinders werk met hulle hande en bou 'n stoel uit hout. Ander luister mooi en weet wat om vir 'n hartseer maat te sê. Iemand anders hanteer diere rustig en leer sy hond om te sit. Op die sportveld hardloop party kinders vinniger as die res van die klas.
items.blok: Nie net in die klaskamer nie
items.bron: Widener University, 'Identifying My Strengths' worksheet (sites.widener.edu): lists mechanical, social, athletic and artistic strengths alongside academic ones. Understood.org, 'Types of strengths in kids': some strengths are obvious (drawing, sport) and others are harder to spot (being a good listener). Checked as a set: all four items are genuine kinds of strength, and none is presented as the opposite of another.

items.bewering: Op die sportveld hardloop party kinders vinniger as die res van die klas.
items.blok: Nie net in die klaskamer nie
items.bron: This is a comparative ('faster than the rest') and is recorded here as a superlative. It is said of 'party kinders' (some children) as a group, so it claims nothing about one fastest child. Running speed differs between children (Widener University and Understood.org, above, list athletic strengths as a category). Correct as written.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense het meer as een sterkpunt, en nie elke sterkpunt lê in die klaskamer nie.
items.blok: Nie net in die klaskamer nie
items.bron: VIA Institute on Character (viacharacter.org) and the VIA Pro practitioner's guide: everyone has all 24 character strengths in different degrees, and a person's top 4 to 7 are counted as 'signature strengths'. That supports 'die meeste ... meer as een', and the quantifier is, if anything, cautious. The Widener University worksheet supports the second half (social, athletic and mechanical strengths outside schoolwork).

items.bewering: Party kinders maak hulle sterkpunt af asof dit niks is nie.
items.bron: Book review of Linley's 'Average to A+' (Brookes University, radar.brookes.ac.uk): research shows only about a third of people can give a meaningful answer about their own strengths. People commonly fail to recognise or credit their strengths. The claim is limited to 'party' (some), so it is a weak claim and is supported.

items.bewering: Dit is iets wat jy kan gebruik, waarop jy kan bou en waarmee jy ander kan help. Daarom gebruik jy jou sterkpunt gereeld en oefen jy dit verder.
items.bron: Gallup CliftonStrengths (gallup.com): a strength is built through continued investment, meaning practice and developing skill. UN Geneva strengths slides (learning.unog.ch): 'use' (how often you use a strength) is one of the three dimensions of a realised strength. VIA (viacharacter.org): signature strengths are ones a person 'frequently exercises'.

items.bewering: Sy sterkpunt vat niks weg van wat jy self kan doen nie.
items.bron: This is a logical claim rather than an empirical one: one person's ability does not lower another person's. It agrees with VIA's model (viacharacter.org), in which each person has their own complete strengths profile, measured separately from anyone else's.

items.bewering: Vertel hom presies wat hy goed gedoen het, nie net dat hy goed is nie.
items.bron: CDC, 'Tips for Using Praise and Rewards' (cdc.gov/parenting-toddlers/responding-to-behavior/using-rewards.html): specific ('labeled') praise works best because it tells the child exactly what they did that earned approval, while general praise does not. Mueller and Dweck (1998), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (columbia.edu PDF): fifth graders praised for their ability did worse after failure than those praised for their effort. The lesson's contrast ('what he did' against 'that he is good') matches both sources. One caveat for the record: a 2016 field experiment (dare.uva.nl) found that labelled praise added little over plain praise on compliance. That does not contradict the advice to be specific.

items.bewering: Ayanda hou daarvan om dinge te verduidelik, en sy praat maklik voor mense. Op die skool se voorleesdag het sy opgestaan en 'n hele storie voorgelees. Die klas het stil geluister, en die juffrou het haar prestasie hardop geprys.
items.bron: This is a made-up example, so there is no outside fact to check. I checked whether it hangs together: the strength (speaking easily in front of people) matches the success (reading aloud to the class) and the praise. 'Prestasie' is used in its normal sense (see the begrip item 'prestasie'). Nothing in it is unsafe or false.

items.bewering: By die huis werk Sipho graag met sy hande, en hy maak dinge reg. Daarom het sy oupa hom in die motorhuis laat kyk hoe 'n ou enjin van binne lyk. Hy het niks gewen of klaargemaak nie, maar dit was vir hom baie opwindend.
items.bron: This is a made-up example. I checked whether it hangs together and whether it is safe: an adult is present, the engine is 'old' and he only looks at it, so nothing invites a child to work on a running engine. Checked against the Ayanda example as a pair: the contrast is that success does not have to mean winning or finishing. That is a sound point, consistent with UN Geneva's strengths model (energy and enjoyment count, not only results; learning.unog.ch).

items.bewering: Neo hardloop vinnig, en hy wen dikwels die kort wedlope by die skool. Op die sportdag het hy op die nat gras gegly en laaste gekom. Hy was daardie middag baie kwaad vir homself. Die volgende week het hy weer net so vinnig op die baan gehardloop.
items.bron: This is a made-up example. I checked whether it hangs together: slipping on wet grass is an ordinary, believable cause of a bad race. It gives no safety instruction. 'Dikwels' (often) is suitably limited, so it does not say he always wins.

items.bewering: Een slegte dag vat nie 'n sterkpunt weg nie.
items.bron: Gallup CliftonStrengths, as summarised by Lehigh University (news.lehigh.edu, 'Tapping into talents'): a strength is the ability to perform near-perfectly *consistently*, so it describes a lasting pattern, not one performance. Mueller and Dweck (1998): treating one failure as proof of low ability is the unhelpful response the research warns about. The claim is supported.

items.bewering: Elke kind het sulke dae, ook dié wat gewoonlik goed vaar.
items.bron: This uses a universal quantifier, so it is recorded as a superlative. Brock University, Department of Psychology/health post 'Why failure is in our children's future and why it is a good thing' (brocku.ca/dphwb, 6 May 2025): setbacks are an expected part of every child's development. Big Brothers Big Sisters of Long Island (bbbsli.org): 'Every child experiences setbacks.' What is claimed universally is having bad days, which is true of every child; it is not a claim about any particular result.

items.bewering: Lerato sukkel met die spelwoorde ... Nou teken sy elke moeilike woord se letters groot en netjies. Sy kleur die letters in wat sy dikwels verkeerd kry. Dan draai sy die bladsy om en skryf die woord uit haar kop.
items.blok: Gebruik jou sterkpunt om beter te word
items.bron: Her method combines two established spelling strategies. (1) Highlighting or colouring the tricky part of a word: Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council, 'Spelling recommendations 2025' (informationdirectory.redcar-cleveland.gov.uk), says to highlight the part the child finds hardest and then have the child write the word from memory; a SAGE teaching resource (in.sagepub.com) says the same. (2) Hiding the word and writing it from memory: Look-Say-Cover-Write-Check and its research version, Cover-Copy-Compare (Winthrop University module PDF; Drivas and Drevon 2018, Behavior Analysis in Practice, via PMC), are shown to improve spelling accuracy. The lesson leaves out the final 'check' step, but leaving it out does not make anything it says false.

items.bewering: Lerato gebruik dus 'n sterkpunt om aan 'n swakheid te werk. So verander 'n slegte toets in 'n positiewe leerervaring.
items.blok: Gebruik jou sterkpunt om beter te word
items.bron: McGill Journal of Education review of strengths-based practice (mje.mcgill.ca): working through a child's strengths is a preferred way to address academic difficulties. Gallup says investing in a weakness will not turn it into a strength, but the lesson does not claim it will. It says only that she uses a strength to *work on* a weakness, which is compatible. The lesson also makes no claim about her test results, so it promises nothing that could be false.

items.bewering: sterkpunt: Iets wat jy goed doen en waarin jy nog beter kan word.
items.bron: Gallup CliftonStrengths (gallup.com, 'How to develop and improve strengths'): strengths are developed through ongoing investment. Linley (Brookes University review): a strength enables performance and development. The glossary entry reads correctly on its own and matches the study text word for word.

items.bewering: swakheid: Iets wat vir jou moeilik gaan en wat jy nog moet oefen.
items.bron: Wiktionary (Afrikaans 'swak'): swak = weak, with 'swakheid' listed as a derived noun. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English, 'weakness': a fault or a point someone is bad at. UN Geneva strengths slides (learning.unog.ch): a weakness is an area of 'lower performance'. 'Something you find hard' is a correct child-level gloss, and 'still have to practise' is a fair use of the word, not a false one.

items.bewering: prestasie: Iets goeds wat jy reggekry het en wat vir jou belangrik is.
items.bron: That 'prestasie' means 'achievement' is shown by the paired Afrikaans and English title 'Prestasies' / 'Achievements' in Tydskrif vir Geesteswetenskappe (scielo.org.za, tvg v65n1), and by the cognate Dutch 'prestatie' (Wiktionary: achievement, accomplishment, feat). The definition follows Longman's 'achievement': 'something important that you succeed in doing by your own efforts' (ldoceonline.com). The clause 'wat vir jou belangrik is' therefore has dictionary support. I could not reach an Afrikaans monolingual dictionary entry (WAT/HAT/Viva) online, so the support is the paired title plus the English and Dutch equivalents.

items.bewering: leerervaring: Enige ervaring wat jou iets leer, of dit goed of sleg afgaan.
items.bron: The Glossary of Education Reform (edglossary.org/learning-experience): a learning experience is any interaction, course, program or other experience in which learning takes place. Britannica Dictionary, 'learning': gaining knowledge or skill by, among other things, experiencing something. 'Enige ervaring' matches 'any', and the clause about it going well or badly is consistent with that.

opsomming: All 21 claims hold up against outside sources and the verdict is GOEDGEKEUR. The lesson contains no health or safety instruction and no analogy; the only superlative-type claims are three quantifiers ('faster than the rest', 'most people', 'every child'), each supported. The weakest support is for 'prestasie', resting on English and Dutch dictionaries and a paired Afrikaans and English journal title because I could not reach an Afrikaans dictionary online.
